items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting the sale
of whipped cream chargers to persons under the age of twenty-one
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2819

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting the
sale of whipped cream chargers to persons under the age of twenty-one

 
PURPOSE:

To prevent the sale of whipped cream chargers or whipits to minors.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amend the general business law by adding a new section 399-hh
to define the term "whipped cream charger" as a steel cylinder or
cartridge filled with nitrous oxide, that is commonly used in a whipped
cream dispenser, and defines other common names used to describe this
item.

It provides that no individual or business within the state sell or
offer for sale a whipped cream charger to any person under the age of
twenty-one.

Outlines the violations of a civil penalty of not more than two hundred
fifty dollars for an initial offense and not more than five hundred
dollars for the second and each subsequent offense.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Whipped cream chargers, commonly known as whipits, contain nitrous
oxide. They are sold by the individual canister or by an entire tank.
Tanks are routinely rented or purchased for blowing up balloons. Nitrous
oxide is known to cause hearing loss, liver and kidney damage, limb
spasms, central nervous system or brain damage, bone marrow damage,
heart failure or suffocation.

According to the National Institute on Drug Abuse, 719,000 people age 12
or older reported using inhalants for the first time within the prior 12
months.

In addition, nitrous oxide is highly addictive. Many state dental asso-
ciations have established treatment programs for dentists and dental
hygienists who have found themselves addicted.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019: S. 5151 - Passed Senate.

2020: S. 5151 - Passed Senate.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
On the thirtieth day after it has become a law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2819A

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to prohibiting the
sale of whipped cream chargers to persons under the age of twenty-one

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To prevent the sale of whipped cream chargers to anyone under the age of
twenty-one.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amend the general business law by adding a new section 399-ii
to define the term "whipped cream charger" as a steel cylinder or
cartridge filled with nitrous oxide, that, is commonly used whipped
cream dispenser.  Provides that no individual or business within the
state sell or offer for sale a whipped cream charger to any person under
the age of twenty-one.

Requires proof of legal age be presented prior to allowing an individual
to purchase or receive a shipment of whipped cream chargers. Such iden-
tification need not be required of any individual who reasonably appears
to be at least twenty-five years of age.

Section 2 outlines the violations of a civil penalty of not more than
two hundred fifty dollars for an initial offense and not more than five
hundred dollars for the second and each subsequent offense.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The amended version of the bill removes language from the previous
version that adds commonly used terms for whipped cream chargers. In
addition, the amended version adds in a mechanism that would require
providing proof of legal age in the acquisition of whipped cream char-
gers so that the distributor/seller will have a way of knowing the age
of the consumer.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Whipped. cream chargers, commonly known as whip its, contain nitrous
oxide. They are sold by the individual canister or by an entire tank.
Tanks are routinely rented or purchased for blowing up balloons.
Nitrous oxide is known to cause hearing loss, liver and kidney damage,
limb spasms, central nervous system or brain damage, bone marrow damage,
heart failure or suffocation.  According to the National Institute on
Drug Abuse, 719,000 people age 12 or older reported using inhalants for
the first time within the prior 12 months.

In addition, nitrous oxide is highly addictive. Many state dental asso-
ciations have established treatment programs for dentists and dental
hygienists who have found themselves addicted.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019: S. 5151 - Passed Senate. 2020: S. 5151 - Passed Senate.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
On the thirtieth day after it has become a law.
